wave: CORRECTNESS -- SemanticObservation::raw_observation_id() joined evidence_refs with an unescaped comma, violating its own documented unconditional contract that only an observation identical in every field shares this id with another
wave_title: Thirteenth generation this cycle, returning to correctness/security after the R5 design-synthesis pivot. Delegated a survey scoped to three foundational core/src/semantic/ files (observation.rs, place.rs, diagnostic.rs) referenced piecemeal this cycle (their identity_key() formulas spot-checked) but never read end-to-end for their own internal logic. Its finding was independently re-verified before any change, including tracing exactly which production call sites could and could not currently trigger it.
priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity -- highest category in the standing priority order. A pure function whose own docstring makes an absolute, unconditional identity-uniqueness claim that is provably false via the public API alone (no extractor-specific assumption needed to construct the counterexample) -- the same delimiter-injection class this codebase already recognizes and defends against elsewhere via escape_identity_field, just not yet applied here.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly scoped to core/src/semantic/observation.rs, place.rs, and diagnostic.rs in full. It correctly found place.rs and diagnostic.rs sound (a pure data enum with no computation of its own; a diagnostic id whose only variable field is last in its seed string, so it can never be shifted against the fixed code/dimension prefix) and reported only the raw_observation_id() finding. Independently re-verified before any change: read the real seed() function directly, confirmed EvidenceId::new's real signature (typed_id! macro-generated, impl Into<String>, zero charset restriction) in core/src/identity/mod.rs, confirmed escape_identity_field's real existence and doc comment (already established in this codebase specifically for this delimiter-injection shape), and -- going beyond the subagent's own report -- grepped every production (non-test) EvidenceId::new call site across the whole workspace to determine whether this defect is reachable via any REAL call path today, not merely via the public API in the abstract, before deciding whether it clears this session's own bar against manufacturing narrow/hypothetical defects.
key_finding: raw_observation_id()'s internal seed() helper builds its hash input via evidence_refs.join(",") with no escaping, while EvidenceId (a typed_id!-generated newtype) has zero charset restriction on its wrapped String -- nothing in the type system or any validation path prevents an EvidenceId from containing a literal comma. Two headers differing only in evidence-ref cardinality -- one evidence ref "ev,idence" versus two separate refs "ev" and "idence" -- produce byte-identical seed strings and therefore the identical RawObservationId, directly violating the method's own docstring: "Only an observation identical in every field -- claim identity, extractor id/version, epistemic status, evidence refs, provenance, and the full typed payload -- shares this id with another." Independently confirmed this is NOT reachable via any current production code path (every production EvidenceId::new call site across the whole workspace constructs its value from stable_id(...)'s fixed "{prefix}:{hash:016x}" output, which structurally can never contain a comma), but judged this still clears the bar for a genuine, non-manufactured fix (distinct from a prior generation's correctly-declined orphan-diagnostic finding, which required imagining an entirely new future extractor implementation): this defect is provably reachable via the PUBLIC API alone with no speculative future extractor needed, the function's own docstring states an unconditional (not call-site-scoped) invariant, and this exact defensive pattern is already an established, adopted convention in this codebase (escape_identity_field, already used for DependencyIdentity/DependencyEdge's own composite keys) specifically for this delimiter-injection shape -- applying it here is completing an existing discipline, not inventing a new one.
verification_before_acting: Read the real, current seed() function directly in core/src/semantic/observation.rs, confirming the exact unescaped evidence_refs.join(",") the subagent described.
Read EvidenceId's real definition (the typed_id! macro in core/src/identity/mod.rs) directly, confirming its constructor is a bare impl Into<String> with no charset validation anywhere.

Read escape_identity_field's real implementation and doc comment directly, confirming it already exists in this codebase specifically to prevent this delimiter-injection shape when joining fields the caller cannot prove are separator-free.

Grepped EVERY production (non-test) EvidenceId::new call site across adapter/src, runtime/src, core/src, apps/cli/src (not just the files the subagent looked at) to independently confirm the defect's current unreachability via any real call path, and weighed that finding explicitly against this session's own standing rule against manufacturing narrow/hypothetical defects before deciding to fix it -- judged distinct from a prior generation's correctly-declined orphan-diagnostic gap because this one is reachable via the public API alone (no new extractor needed) and the violated contract is stated as unconditional in the function's own docstring.

design_decisions.question: Fix this now given it is not currently triggered by any real call site, or leave it since no current input reaches it?
design_decisions.decision: Fix it. The function's own docstring states an unconditional guarantee, not one scoped to 'as long as no evidence id ever contains a comma' -- and this codebase already has zero validation anywhere preventing a future evidence-id source (e.g. one incorporating free text rather than the current fixed stable_id format) from reintroducing exactly this collision silently. This mirrors the codebase's own already-adopted principle (escape_identity_field's very existence) that a field the caller cannot PROVE is separator-free must be escaped before joining, rather than trusting today's callers to stay well-behaved forever.

design_decisions.question: Escape only evidence_refs, or also provenance.source_path/extractor (also unescaped in the same format string)?
design_decisions.decision: Scoped narrowly to evidence_refs, matching the survey's own explicit reasoning: source_path is a single field followed by a FIXED extractor-id literal and a numeric line:col span (not a variable-cardinality LIST being joined), so a real collision there would require a contrived, syntactically-improbable file path -- the specific delimiter-injection shape escape_identity_field's own doc comment targets (joining SEVERAL fields with a separator) applies to evidence_refs's Vec, not to source_path's single-field position in the format string.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: raw_observation_id() now escapes each evidence ref before joining with a comma, so an evidence ref containing a literal comma can never become indistinguishable, once joined, from two separate refs split at that same character -- restoring the method's own documented unconditional uniqueness guarantee.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Added an_evidence_ref_containing_a_comma_never_collides_with_a_differently_split_evidence_list, constructing the exact counterexample (one ref "ev,idence" vs. two refs "ev"/"idence") via the public EvidenceId::new constructor alone. Falsified per this session's standing discipline: backed up the file, reverted the fix to the original unescaped join, ran the new test, confirmed it failed with the exact expected collision (both sides producing the identical RawObservationId("raw-observation:7f885d279401ccb1")), then restored the fix from backup (git diff --stat confirmed the restored file exactly matched the fix) and confirmed the test passes.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: cargo fmt --all --check: clean. cargo test --workspace: 555 total (296 adapter, 5 apps/cli, 174 core, 80 runtime), 0 failed -- up from 554 (+1 new test). docs audit --root .atlas: gate_ready true.

implementation.code_change: core/src/semantic/observation.rs -- raw_observation_id()'s internal seed() helper now maps each evidence_refs entry through escape_identity_field(id.as_str(), ',') before collecting and joining, instead of collecting raw &str references directly. Added one new test.
implementation.docs_change: NONE -- this closes a gap in already-documented, already-stated behavior (the method's own docstring already claims the unconditional uniqueness guarantee this fix restores); no new architectural concept introduced.

adversarial_and_falsification_coverage: reverted the fix and confirmed the new test fails with the exact expected collision (both differently-structured evidence lists producing the byte-identical RawObservationId) before trusting the fix, using a full file backup/restore cycle (cp before revert, cp restore after, git diff --stat confirming the restored file exactly matched the fix)

went beyond the delegated subagent's own scope by grepping every production EvidenceId::new call site workspace-wide (not just the files it examined) to make an independent, evidenced judgment about whether this defect clears this session's own anti-manufacturing bar, rather than either blindly fixing or blindly declining based on the subagent's framing alone

explicitly reasoned about and declined a broader fix (also escaping provenance.source_path/extractor) after confirming that field's different structural position (single field before a fixed suffix, not a joined variable-cardinality list) does not present the same delimiter-injection shape

confirmed the fix does not regress any of the three pre-existing raw_observation_id-related tests in this file (differing_evidence_refs_change_the_raw_observation_id_..., identical_raw_observations_share_a_raw_observation_id, evidence_refs_accessor_matches_the_wrapped_header) -- all still pass unchanged

cargo test --workspace.totals: 555 total, 0 failed (296 adapter, 5 apps/cli, 174 core, 80 runtime)

recensus_scope_after_promotion: no prior CLOSED/EXTINCT conclusion depended on this collision being unnoticed, so no external conclusion requires reopening -- no current production evidence-id source can trigger it (confirmed by the workspace-wide grep above), so this fix is preventive of a currently-latent-but-real contract violation rather than a fix to an already-observed production symptom

the same survey confirmed core/src/semantic/place.rs (PlaceRef) and core/src/semantic/diagnostic.rs (ExtractionDiagnostic id construction) are both sound -- genuinely clean, not a gap, consistent with this session's own discipline against manufacturing a second finding to pad the report

if a future evidence-id source is ever introduced that is not stable_id-shaped (e.g. one incorporating free text, a file path, or a user-authored string), this fix is the reason that source would not silently corrupt raw-observation dedup the way it would have before this generation
overall_verdict: FIXED, FALSIFIED, AND VERIFIED. raw_observation_id() now escapes each evidence ref before joining, restoring its own documented unconditional uniqueness guarantee and closing a real delimiter-injection defect reachable via the public EvidenceId API alone, judged non-manufactured because the violated contract is stated as unconditional in the function's own docstring and the fix completes an already-established codebase convention (escape_identity_field) rather than inventing a new one. Falsified via full backup-revert-confirm-restore. Full workspace test suite green (555/555).
